Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

decrease verb and noun

also go down, get smaller, become less, lessen, diminish, wane, reduction, fall (in number or amount)

classical

Cic. Sen. 21: at memoria minuitur
Cic. Off. 1.123: senibus autem labōrēs corporis minuendī

minuō, minuere, minuī, minūtum

verb, third conjugation, transitive; in the passive, to grow less

make less, lessen; in the passive, decrease

Transitive: to make less (see make smaller); the passive is the everyday “to go down, grow less”.

Other words

  • dēcrēscō, dēcrēscere, dēcrēvī, dēcrētum — decrease, grow less, wane

    verb, third conjugation, intransitive · classical · Hor. C. 4.7.3: dēcrēscentia rīpās flūmina praetereunt; Cic. Div. 2.33: ostreae cum lūnā pariter crēscunt pariterque dēcrēscunt (Lewis & Short)

    Of what grows less of itself: rivers going down, the waning moon (dēcrēscente lūnā, Col. 12.47.2), a fever; the opposite of crēscō.

  • dēminuō, dēminuere, dēminuī, dēminūtum — lessen by taking away, reduce

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 1.53.6: neque dē tantā voluptāte et grātulātiōne quicquam fortūna dēminuerat (Lewis & Short); Tac. Agr. 9.4: aut sevēritās amōrem dēminuit

    To make less by taking something away (dē): with dē or ex and the ablative, to take away from.

  • dēminūtiō, dēminūtiōnis f. — a decrease, a reduction

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1, 28: accrētiō et dēminūtiō lūminis (Lewis & Short); Cic. Agr. 1.21: vectīgālium (Lewis & Short)

    The noun, in good prose (Lewis & Short); a decrease in revenue, in numbers, in rank.

Examples

  • at memoria minuitur. crēdō, nisi eam exerceās

    “But memory fades.” — I suppose so, unless you exercise itCic. Sen. 21

  • mūtat terra vicēs et dēcrēscentia rīpās flūmina praetereunt

    the earth goes through its changes, and the rivers, going down, flow past within their banksHor. C. 4.7.3–4

  • nec illī, quod est rārissimum, aut facilitās auctōritātem aut sevēritās amōrem dēminuit

    in him, the rarest thing, neither his easiness lessened his authority nor his strictness affectionTac. Agr. 9.4

See also increase, make smaller, less.
